message.content:
**Hydrogen – A Quick Reference Guide to Its Properties**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Atomic Data** | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Ionization energy (first) | 13.598 eV |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV (negative, so it does *not* readily accept an electron) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Atomic radius | ~31 pm (covalent) |
| | Nuclear spin | ½ (proton) |
| | Magnetic moment | 2.7928 µ_N (nuclear) |
| **Physical State (STP)** | State | Gas |
| | Color | Colorless |
| | Odor | Odorless |
| | Taste | Tasteless |
| | Density | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (at 0 °C, 1 atm) |
| | Molar volume | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (121 K) |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (14 K) |
| | Specific heat (gas) | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (at 25 °C) |
| | Thermal conductivity | 180 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ (at 25 °C) |
| | Diffusivity | ~0.0002 m² s⁻¹ (fastest among gases) |
| | Solubility in water | 1.6 × 10⁻³ mol L⁻¹ (at 25 °C) |
| **Chemical Properties** | Diatomic molecule | H₂ (most stable form) |
| | Bond dissociation energy (H–H) | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Flammability | Extremely flammable; explosive mixture with air (4–75 % H₂ in air) |
| | Reactivity with halogens | Forms hydrogen halides (HF, HCl, HBr, HI) |
| | Reaction with oxygen | Combustion → H₂O (exothermic) |
| | Acidic behavior | Weak acid (HF) when bonded to fluorine; otherwise neutral |
| | Basicity | None (does not act as a base) |
| | Hydride formation | Forms metal hydrides (e.g., LiH, NaH) |
| | Oxidation states | +1 (as H⁺), –1 (as H⁻) |
| | Redox potential | 0 V vs. SHE for H⁺/H₂ couple |
| **Isotopic Variants** | Protium (¹H) | Most common (≈99.98 %) |
| | Deuterium (²H, D) | Stable isotope; heavier (mass ≈2 u); used in NMR, heavy water |
| | Tritium (³H, T) | Radioactive (β‑emitter, half‑life ≈12.32 yr); used in fusion research |
| **Nuclear & Astrophysical** | Fusion reaction | 2 ¹H → ²He (protium) → ³He → ⁴He (helium) |
| | Role in stars | Primary fuel in stellar nucleosynthesis; powers the proton–proton chain |
| | Abundance | ~75 % of baryonic mass in the universe; most abundant element |
| | Spectral lines | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible) – key in astronomy |
| **Applications & Uses** | Fuel cell technology | Hydrogen fuel cells produce electricity + water |
| | Industrial processes | Ammonia synthesis (Haber process), methanol production, refining |
| | Space propulsion | Liquid hydrogen + liquid oxygen as rocket propellant |
| | Medical imaging | Deuterated compounds in NMR spectroscopy |
| | Energy storage | Hydrogen storage (compressed, liquefied, metal hydrides) |
| | Research & education | Model system for quantum mechanics, chemistry, and physics |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element**: Hydrogen is the simplest atom, consisting of one proton and one electron.
- **Highly reactive**: It readily forms bonds with many elements, especially halogens and oxygen.
- **Flammable**: Hydrogen gas is extremely flammable and can form explosive mixtures with air.
- **Isotopic diversity**: Protium, deuterium, and tritium each have distinct physical and nuclear properties.
- **Astrophysical importance**: Hydrogen fuels stars and dominates the elemental composition of the cosmos.
- **Technological relevance**: From fuel cells to rocket propellants, hydrogen plays a pivotal role in modern energy solutions.

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property or application!

Also physical properties: colorless, odorless, tasteless gas at STP, low density, high diffusivity, etc. Also chemical properties: forms hydrides, reacts with halogens, etc. Also nuclear properties: nuclear spin, magnetic moment.
